General build taken from custom_mmus_hsc.Rmd etc. 

Similarly to before this script will be used to recluster and annotate 
one of the published datasets, in this case tabula sapiens fetal HSPCs.

This time, I will perform the standard clustering pipeline, but 

 - FIRST subset to signature gene orthologs only,

 - THEN perform batch correction (or I'd need to calculate variable features),

 - THEN cluster with the same resolution used for the non-batch-corrected
signature-based reclustering, 

 - and THEN do a blind annotation.

This is to show the effect of batch correction as would be done in a 
normal preprocessing pipeline.

Again, I will save the resulting object from within this script 
for simplicity reasons.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

# Batch correction and clustering

```{r resolution}
# get the resolution used to recluster the same object with signature genes
# but without batch-correction
resolution <- resolution_df %>%
  dplyr::filter(dataset == "ts_hscs_progenitors") %>%
  dplyr::filter(conservation_level == "conserved_signature") %>%
  dplyr::pull()
resolution
```

Similar to the seurat pipeline roughly taken from sce_functions_reclustering.R
The seurat object should be pretty basic.

Adding a step for batch correction. 
Still keeping it very basic here.
Sticking to this vignette: https://satijalab.org/seurat/archive/v4.3/integration_introduction
because the original clustering was done in Seurat v4.3.0

```{r subset}

# subset right from the beginnging
# this is because if variable or integration features are calculated, 
# they will not include enough/all signature genes
# seems a little silly but this also seems to be the best option right now

ensembl_column_use <- seu_ts_hscs_progenitors@misc$ensembl_column_use
ensembl_column_use

length(unique(ensembl_sign$MMUS_SYMBOL)) # there are 229 signature genes

sign_ids <- unique(ensembl_sign[,ensembl_column_use])
length(sign_ids) # and 226 features that are orthologs of those
table(sign_ids %in% rownames(seu_ts_hscs_progenitors)) # of which 224 are in the object's rownames

# subset seurat_object 
seu_ts_hscs_progenitors_sub <- seu_ts_hscs_progenitors[
  rownames(seu_ts_hscs_progenitors) %in% sign_ids,]
```

```{r seurat_clustering_pipeline_split}

# start from raw data
seu_ts_hscs_progenitors_sub@misc$data_use 

seu_ts_hscs_progenitors_list <- Seurat::SplitObject(
  seu_ts_hscs_progenitors_sub, 
  split.by = "assay")
# unlike ts_bone_marrow, there are many fetal donors from many different stages 
# so instead I'd like to try assay first which was the main cause of cell type
# separation in figure 4
# also, there SHOULD be biological differences between some cell type of diff-
# erent fetal stages so not sure that overcorrecting those away are a good idea

# normalize and identify variable features for each dataset independently
seu_ts_hscs_progenitors_list <- lapply(
  X = seu_ts_hscs_progenitors_list, 
  FUN = function(seu){
    
    seu <- Seurat::NormalizeData(
      seu, 
      assay = "RNA", 
      verbose = FALSE)

    seu <- Seurat::FindVariableFeatures(
      seu, 
      selection.method = "vst", 
      nfeatures = nrow(seu)) # just use all genes

    return(seu)
})
seu_ts_hscs_progenitors_list
```

```{r seurat_clustering_pipeline_integration}
# start integration

int_features <- Seurat::SelectIntegrationFeatures(
  object.list = seu_ts_hscs_progenitors_list)
length(int_features) 

anchors_ts_hscs_progenitors <- Seurat::FindIntegrationAnchors(
  object.list = seu_ts_hscs_progenitors_list,
  anchor.features = int_features,
  verbose = FALSE)

combined_ts_hscs_progenitors <- Seurat::IntegrateData(
  anchorset = anchors_ts_hscs_progenitors,
  verbose = FALSE)

dim(combined_ts_hscs_progenitors)
combined_ts_hscs_progenitors
```

```{r seurat_clustering_pipeline_downstream}
# run the downstream analysis on the integrated data
DefaultAssay(combined_ts_hscs_progenitors) <- "integrated"

combined_ts_hscs_progenitors <- Seurat::ScaleData(
  combined_ts_hscs_progenitors, 
  verbose = FALSE)

# uses scaled data
combined_ts_hscs_progenitors <- Seurat::RunPCA(
  combined_ts_hscs_progenitors,
  npcs = 30,
  verbose = FALSE)
  
# check and possibly define nr of pcs
nr_pca <- ncol(combined_ts_hscs_progenitors@reductions$pca)
print(nr_pca)

# requires PC coordinates
combined_ts_hscs_progenitors <- Seurat::FindNeighbors(
  combined_ts_hscs_progenitors, 
  reduction = "pca",
  dims = 1:nr_pca, 
  verbose = FALSE)
  
# requires neighbors
combined_ts_hscs_progenitors <- Seurat::FindClusters(
  combined_ts_hscs_progenitors, 
  resolution = as.numeric(resolution), 
  verbose = FALSE) 

# calculate UMAP
combined_ts_hscs_progenitors <-  Seurat::RunUMAP(
  combined_ts_hscs_progenitors,
  dims = 1:10)
combined_ts_hscs_progenitors
```

Now continue with the blind annotation.

# Blind annotation

## Calculate markers

```{r marker_list}
clust_list <- as.list(levels(combined_ts_hscs_progenitors$seurat_clusters))

ct_markers_ts_hscs_progenitors <- lapply(clust_list, function(x){
  markers <- Seurat::FindMarkers(combined_ts_hscs_progenitors,
                                 test.use = "wilcox",
                                 ident.1 = x)

  markers <- markers[base::order(base::abs(markers$avg_log2FC), 
                                 decreasing=TRUE),]

  markers$which_cluster <- base::rep(x, nrow(markers))
  markers <- rownames_to_column(markers, var = "genes")
  
  # need to add only ensembl gene symbols as I will not be using others
  markers$symbol <- markers$genes
  markers$symbol <- ensembl_sign$HSAPIENS_SYMBOL[
    base::match(markers$genes, ensembl_sign$ENSG_ID)]

  return(markers)
})
names(ct_markers_ts_hscs_progenitors) <- levels(combined_ts_hscs_progenitors$seurat_clusters)

combined_ts_hscs_progenitors$batchc_sign_labels <- vector(length = ncol(combined_ts_hscs_progenitors))
```

Will go in the order of 1, 7, 0, 8 (interspersed with 0), 3, 6, 2, 5, 4.

### Show markers

```{r cluster1}
nr <- "1"
markers <- ct_markers_ts_hscs_progenitors[[nr]]$genes[
  !is.na(ct_markers_ts_hscs_progenitors[[nr]]$symbol) &
    ct_markers_ts_hscs_progenitors[[nr]]$avg_log2FC > 0 &
    ct_markers_ts_hscs_progenitors[[nr]]$p_val_adj < 0.05]

ct_markers_ts_hscs_progenitors[[nr]][
  !is.na(ct_markers_ts_hscs_progenitors[[nr]]$symbol) & 
    ct_markers_ts_hscs_progenitors[[nr]]$avg_log2FC > 0 &
    ct_markers_ts_hscs_progenitors[[nr]]$p_val_adj < 0.05,][c(1, 3, 6, 8)]

Seurat::FeaturePlot(combined_ts_hscs_progenitors, markers[1:6])
Seurat::FeaturePlot(combined_ts_hscs_progenitors, markers[7:12])
# HLF, CD34, MSI2, MECOM, MPL among the top genes are major HSC genes

combined_ts_hscs_progenitors$batchc_sign_labels[
  combined_ts_hscs_progenitors$seurat_clusters == nr] <- "HSC"
```
